verified.summary: Scope checks out. The ref feat/br-2026-10-04-p0-queue/phase-4 resolves to 4fe2e7b, which is also the worktree HEAD. The three-dot diff has 53 files, 10 of them under app/. Of the 8 findings, 7 hold up against the tree and 1 is refuted. None is CRITICAL or HIGH, and none involves anything that freezes at merge (no migrations, schemas or wire formats). The two MEDIUMs are a missing Bear-side test (three mutants that record or show the wrong side get through the whole suite) and live Ask results hidden by the crowd panel while the keyboard is open. The rest are LOW: test-strength gaps, fixtures that disagree with the Markets tab, and a scroll offset that stays clamped after narrowing the filter. Nothing must be fixed before merge. The Bear-side test is the cheapest worthwhile fix and should go in first.

refuted.title: Ask matches only the ticker, so asking by asset name falsely reports no battle
refuted.reason: The spec says to filter by 'asset/ticker substring', and the same spec defines `asset` as a Battle field. Battle.asset is the ticker ('BTC'), and asked() does a substring match on it, exactly as written. The no-match state then shows 'Try BTC, ETH, SOL', which is the spec-mandated hint pointing users to tickers, so the user is not misled. Matching full names (TradeMock.quotes[...].name) would be a feature extension, not a defect in this diff.

checked: Scope: feat/br-2026-10-04-p0-queue/phase-4 resolves to 4fe2e7b. The worktree HEAD is that commit on that branch. The three-dot diff lists 53 files, including app/lib changes.

Participant count is keyed by actionId. Scenario.joins counts receipts by clashId+side. placeOrder returns the existing receipt for a repeated actionId before any write (scenario.dart:165-167), and the participation write sits after the receipt write and after problem() and the stale-price failure, so duplicate confirms, failures and trader-index refusals add nothing. Cancel and Done only pop.

A rested limit or stop order opened from an Arena ticket returns OrderResting before the receipt/participation write. Its toast ('Limit long placed · in Open orders (simulated)') is truthful and counts no join. No other code writes openOrders, positions or receipts, so no later fill path can lose the clash.

Two battles cannot share an actionId. _newActionId is one library-level counter ('act-N') shared by order_ticket.dart and its part feed_order_ticket.dart, and is minted once per ticket open. No seeded order or position uses an 'act-' id. reset clears receipts while the counter keeps rising, so nothing collides after a reset.

clashId plumbing: the arena card (arena_screen.dart:127-128) and the opinions dock (opinions_screen.dart:141-152) pass symbol b.asset, side and clashId b.id. OrderTicket._intent carries widget.clashId, and Retry's requote reuses _intent, so the clashId survives a retry. placeOrder stores it on both OrderReceipt and PortfolioPosition (data field only, accepted).
Flipping the side inside the ticket records the side actually filled: participation and the count both follow intent.side, which is truthful.

No battle can reach the ticket as a trader market: BTC, ETH and SOL are all in TradeMock.quotes and none is stale (stalePrices = {AVAX}). Had one been a handle, the ticket closes with the not-built toast and records nothing.

Participation and arena are static ValueNotifiers, so they survive navigation. Scenario.reset clears both (participation = {}, arena = allBattles), and resetDemo calls Scenario.reset. The Ask field's _followQuery listener clears the text on reset.
VC-ARN-005: setArena writes only Scenario.arena. Sort, range and Ask changes touch no receipt, position, order or participation.

Derived percentages on the opinions header ('Crowd split N% bull') and dock ('Crowd split · N opinions') and on the panel label ('Crowd split a/b') are labelled crowd split. No 'odds' or 'probability' appears in the arena code.
The askHint 'Try BTC, ETH, SOL' is derived from ArenaMock.battles assets, sorted.
The battle card colours a '−'-prefixed change as negative (vista_battle.dart:113), so the new negative ETH change renders correctly.
notExamined: Did not run flutter tests; relied on gate facts given (233 pass both configs) and source reading.

findings.fix: Fold the crowd panel away while the keyboard is open. findings.title: Narrowing the crowd range while the list is scrolled keeps the clamped scroll offset, so the remaining card opens with its header scrolled away
findings.failurePath: Route: Arena at 360x640 @1.3. Scroll the battle list to the end, then narrow the crowd range to a single bucket (from 7 to 8, SOL only). The ListView keeps its position, clamped to the new max extent: offset 228 px in a 281 px viewport. The one remaining SOL card shows from mid-card down, and its ticker, price and question sit above the viewport. At 375x667 @1.3 the offset is 197; at 1.0 it is 135 and 104. Count and list agree (panel '1 battle', 1 card) and nothing throws, so this is presentation only.
findings.fix: Give the ListView a ScrollController and jump it to 0 when the sort or range changes. For example, in `_battles`, compare view.from, view.to and view.sort against the last values and call `_scroll.jumpTo(0)` in a post-frame callback. Or key the ListView on `(view.sort, view.from, view.to)` so it rebuilds at the top.
